caption:
TL;DR: Rockets launch east to borrow Earth's spin: over 900 mph at Cape Canaveral, plus an ocean to fly over.

One-liner: "Rockets go east because Earth is already moving that way."

Knowledge pearl: Not every rocket goes east. NASA says Vandenberg in California is preferred for north-south, or polar, orbits.

youtube_title: Why Rockets Launch East From Florida: a Free 900 mph
youtube_description:
Why do rockets launch east from Florida? Earth spins toward the east, so a rocket at Cape Canaveral is already moving over 900 mph before liftoff.
Launching west would turn that bonus into a penalty, and launching east sends rockets out over the Atlantic instead of over towns. By simple math, that bonus is about 5% of orbital speed (~17,500 mph, the space station's speed) for a due-east launch.
